text:
jo: Quick report — customer using Cloudflare Workers (Pages) and our JS SDK hit multiple failures. Main ones: bundler pulled in process/Buffer, types fail under lib:webworker, and subtle.digest missing in one older runtime.

kevin: Repro we used in miniflare: import('@redwood/inference') inside a worker and the bundle contained a tiny process shim that caused runtime ReferenceError for other globals. Vite ended up optimizing a transitive dep that referenced `process.nextTick`.

marie: I tried a short hack: publish a dedicated entrypoint `@redwood/inference/edge` that points at dist/esm-edge/index.mjs and set package.json exports so browsers/edge prefer it. That solved most runtime leaks.

priya: Important nuance on types: our public retry helper still mentions `NodeJS.Timeout` and `stream.Readable`. That breaks tsc when users set `lib: ["webworker"]`. We should ship edge-only .d.ts and change the types to be DOM-friendly (use ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> or number, and use ReadableStream instead of Node streams).

jo: Also discovered a surprising runtime difference: Cloudflare Workers has structuredClone and a global fetch that behaves slightly differently; some of our internal helpers used lodash.deepClone and stream.Readable assumptions. For the edge build we should prefer native web primitives (structuredClone, ReadableStream) to avoid pulling Node libs.

kevin: Bundlers are tricky: Vite/rollup sometimes inject `process.env.NODE_ENV` which drags in process polyfills. Recommend two things:
1) Provide an edge ESM build that is pure ESM with no commonjs fallback.
2) In docs recommend build flags for common bundlers (esbuild --platform=browser, vite: define process.env = {} and optimizeDeps.exclude). Include quick copy-paste snippets in examples.

marie: About crypto: prefer feature-detecting `globalThis.crypto?.subtle` and only export a tiny fallback `digestSha256` that uses a small JS hash only if subtle absent. Do not bundle fast-webcrypto by default. Make the fallback tree-shakeable so advanced users can replace it.

priya: On AbortController: earlier runtimes lacked a complete AbortController. We can ship a guarded minimal shim that sets signal.aborted and provides abort(), but we must document the limitations (it doesn't cancel underlying TCP in some runtimes). Keep it opt-in or only attach when absent.

jo: Proposal summary to implement:
- add dist/esm-edge build (ESM, platform browser, no CJS shims)
- package.json exports map with an explicit "./edge" subpath and conditional exports so bundlers pick edge by default for browser consumers
- split .d.ts into node vs edge and point via exports -> types
- tiny opt-in edge-shims module (no Buffer, no Node APIs) and example worker showing how to include it
- update docs with bundler recipes and miniflare/wrangler smoke tests in CI

kevin: I'll open PR for the build + exports map. PR will add examples/workers/minimal.mjs and a miniflare test that just imports the edge entry and calls a mocked token endpoint. Tagging @priya for d.ts adjustments.

priya: I'll update the types in a follow-up: remove NodeJS.Timer from public surface, add `types/edge/index.d.ts`, and change any stream types to ReadableStream in edge defs. Also update onboarding docs to recommend `import {createClient} from "@redwood/inference/edge"` for Cloudflare deploys.

miniflare-bot: ci: queued workers-edge-smoke #8902

marie: Action items assigned: kevin -> PR for edge build + examples; priya -> types + docs; jo -> update onboarding checklist and escalate to support for impacted customer. We'll keep shims minimal and opt-in. Label thread `edge-dx` and `sdk-js`. :white_check_mark:
